notes: §1985:VII.3.2.2 prints FD file-name-1 with the optional BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD (three forms), LABEL {RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE} {STANDARD | OMITTED}, VALUE OF {implementor-name-1 IS {data-name-2 | literal-1}} ..., DATA {RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE} {data-name-3} ..., LINAGE and CODE-SET clauses and a period, and §1985:VII.3.2.3 SR2 says 'The clauses which follow file-name-1 may appear in any order.' fileDescriptionEntry takes the clauses in any order; the operand gap of the prior PARTIAL read is closed (kb/Work PB5070 landed): labelRecordsClause now ends in (STANDARD | OMITTED) and valueOfClause is VALUE OF valueOfEntry+ with valueOfEntry = word IS? (literal | data reference); BindFileSection binds each clause through FileDescriptionClauseAdmitted and the Bind* members, ScreenDataRecords checks DATA RECORDS names (COBOL6849), ScreenClauseRepetition refuses a repeated clause, VisitUnrecognizedDataClause any other word, and the 2002-or-later additions are refused at 85 in VisitRecordClause and VisitCodeSetClause. Probed at --std 85: (b) LABEL RECORDS ARE IGNORED, LABEL RECORD IS LBL1 LBL2, VALUE OF "FX", VALUE OF ID IS (no operand), LABEL written twice (COBOL2423), RECORD written twice, DATA RECORD IS Q (no such 01), RECORDING MODE F, LINAGE ... TOP before FOOTING, a missing period and an FD with no record description (COBOL1837, SR3) are refused; (c) EXTERNAL AS "XX", RECORD CONTAINS 8 BYTES (COBOL0900) and CODE-SET ... FOR refused; (e) LINAGE on a RELATIVE file refused COBOL2604; an FD with all seven clauses, the same clauses reordered with every optional word dropped (VALUE OF ID "FX", DATA RECORDS R, LABEL RECORD OMITTED), an FD with no clause, BLOCK CONTAINS 2 TO 2 RECORDS and RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON WN compile and run, reading back what was written; at --std 2002 LABEL, VALUE OF and DATA RECORDS are refused as removed. The witness writes BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD CONTAINS, LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD and DATA RECORD IS on one FD and reads two records back. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5070 (landed), kb/Work PB5115 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5070 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09-refute.json).

next.reason: §1985:VII.3.2.2, the sequential file description entry, writes out BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD, LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF, DATA RECORDS, LINAGE and CODE-SET. Its 2023 counterpart is §2023:13.4.5.2 'Format 1 (sequential)', which §2023:13.4.5.3 SR5 names ('Format 1 is the file description entry for a sequential file'); it writes BLOCK CONTAINS and CODE-SET in line and takes the RECORD and LINAGE clauses by reference to §2023:13.18.43.2 and §2023:13.18.34.2. It has no LABEL RECORDS, VALUE OF or DATA RECORDS clause (in 1985 the subjects of §1985:VII.3.2.4 GR2, 'the DATA RECORDS clause, the LABEL RECORDS clause'), so a 1985 FD using them is refused; it also adds FORMAT and a wider CODE-SET. A compile-time difference, no exception condition: CHANGED. The clause-order rule carries its own record (1985 SR2). The BLOCK CONTAINS and CODE-SET clauses Format 1 writes in line are restated by their own clause formats, §2023:13.18.10.2 and §2023:13.18.13.2, which therefore state part of the entry's syntax too.
